compute_budget.time_budget_scope: Grid/Arrangement/BnB search stages; exact feasibility and bound certificates run to completion and may extend total runtime

optimization.upper_bound_method: Rational Steiner enclosure over decimalized represented usable geometry
optimization.optimality_scope: all translations and orientations of the declared rectangular lattice family within the decimalized represented usable polygon; conditional on a passing exact-rational lattice relation and usable-geometry feasibility certificate

rational_lattice_relation.spacing_proof: For distinct integer index pairs, the exact squared separation is m^2*a^2+n^2*b^2 because the certified basis is orthogonal; it is therefore at least min(a,b)^2.
limitations: This certifies membership in the declared rational orthogonal lattice, not CRS correctness or field feasibility.

source_constraint_feasibility.arithmetic: exact rational arithmetic on canonical decimal inputs; no epsilon in point-in-polygon or squared-distance comparisons
source_constraint_feasibility.input_interpretation: decimal strings/integers are exact; finite floats are interpreted by their shortest round-trip decimal string
source_constraint_feasibility.geometry_scope: GeoJSON Polygon/MultiPolygon, including interior rings (holes); MultiPolygon components must be strictly disjoint and non-touching
source_constraint_feasibility.clearance_policy: required_clearance = declared_clearance + explicitly supplied uncertainty allowance; no uncertainty is inferred
limitations: This certifies feasibility of the finite submitted candidate set relative to the serialized source geometry and declared margins; it does not certify global optimality.
CRS/datum correctness, survey accuracy, source provenance, and whether uncertainty allowances are adequate require separate gates.
MultiPolygon components that touch or cross are rejected rather than normalized.
Input decimal values are treated as exact mathematical values; this is not a claim about physical measurement truth.

represented_usable_geometry_feasibility.arithmetic: exact rational arithmetic on canonical decimal inputs; no epsilon in point-in-polygon or squared-distance comparisons
represented_usable_geometry_feasibility.input_interpretation: decimal strings/integers are exact; finite floats are interpreted by their shortest round-trip decimal string
represented_usable_geometry_feasibility.geometry_scope: GeoJSON Polygon/MultiPolygon, including interior rings (holes); MultiPolygon components must be strictly disjoint and non-touching
represented_usable_geometry_feasibility.clearance_policy: required_clearance = declared_clearance + explicitly supplied uncertainty allowance; no uncertainty is inferred
limitations: This certifies feasibility of the finite submitted candidate set relative to the serialized source geometry and declared margins; it does not certify global optimality.
CRS/datum correctness, survey accuracy, source provenance, and whether uncertainty allowances are adequate require separate gates.
MultiPolygon components that touch or cross are rejected rather than normalized.
Input decimal values are treated as exact mathematical values; this is not a claim about physical measurement truth.

rational_lattice.coordinate_representation: exact fractions in x_m/y_m; x_m_display/y_m_display are presentation-only
rational_lattice.angle_note: The certified orientation is the exact rational rotation induced by q, which approximates theta_source_deg_display_only; it is not asserted to be mathematically identical to the floating search angle.

notices: The rational lattice relation, source-constraint feasibility, and represented-usable-geometry feasibility are separate certificates.

An optimality conclusion is issued only when the exact-rational feasible lattice lower bound matches the certified upper bound for the same declared rectangular lattice family and represented usable geometry.
Survey/CRS provenance, uncertainty adequacy, agronomic approval, and field validation are separate gates; deployment remains unauthorized.
The finite search result is a lower bound. The certified upper bound applies to the declared rectangular lattice family over the decimalized represented usable polygon.
An exact-feasibility certificate for a finite lattice candidate does not prove the candidate set is complete; equality with the certified upper bound is required for an optimum claim.
Field deployment remains unauthorized pending survey/CRS/uncertainty QA and agronomist approval.
